summary: Tenant rollout stutter causes interleaved fallback paths and mixed-model responses
description:
Issue summary: During a staged model rollout for customer VerdeCommerce we observed repeated short-duration rollouts ('stutters') where a subset of tenant requests were intermittently rerouted to fallback variants despite an explicit model_pin. Impact: Customers reported mixed output quality and unexpected model variant responses for ~20% of requests to a single tenant. This is causing user-facing regressions in the customer's chat assistant and has been elevated by the CS team.

Impact: Mixed-model outputs for production traffic, increased error-monitoring noise, measurable QoE regressions in downstream application A/B checks (customer reported higher complaint rate). No data exfiltration. The behavior started after a canary weight increase that ran at 2026-03-10T08:12:00Z.

Environment: Dedicated pool for VerdeCommerce in prod:us-east-1 using pinned model redwood-v2.0-rc with orchestrator rollout configured as weighted canary (weights: 80 -> 100 over 30m). Edge tier uses header-based affinity and a short-lived session lease (ttl=90s).

Observed behavior: When canary weight increased stepwise, we see transient "stutter" windows (~5-30s) where requests belonging to the pinned tenant alternate between the pinned variant and a fallback variant (open-m-7b). These windows correlate with orchestrator snapshot commits and a flurry of health probe events. Requests during the stutter frequently contained identical session tokens but received different model variants.

Expected behavior: Tenant with explicit model_pin should remain routed to pinned variant for the life of the session lease and during gradual weight changes; fallbacks should be triggered only on persistent capacity or health failures, not during snapshot/commit churn.

Attachments: request-ids, sample payloads, and timing traces attached in ticket artifacts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a weighted canary rollout from redwood-v2.0-rc (pinned) to redwood-v2.0-rc promoted -> full in dedicated pool in us-east-1
2) Use a sustained low-throughput traffic generator with tenant header X-Tenant-ID set to VerdeCommerce and session cookie TTL=90s
3) Step canary weight from 80% to 100% in 10% increments every 5 minutes and observe routing decisions at edge and orchestrator during commit windows
4) Correlate routing logs with orchestrator commit timestamps and edge affinity lease renewals
logs: 2026-03-10T08:12:06Z ORCH[orchestrator-3] INFO commit=sha:7f9b snapshot=451 weight-update from=80 to=90
2026-03-10T08:12:06Z EDGE[proxy-12] WARN tenant=verde session=abc123 route=fallback:open-m-7b reason=route-recompute
2026-03-10T08:15:02Z EDGE[proxy-07] INFO tenant=verde session=def456 route=fallback:open-m-7b reason=kvcache-miss
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Snapshot commit and route recompute is briefly dropping affinity for sessions whose lease is near expiry, causing edge to apply default fallback logic.
Hypothesis B: Orchestrator commit latency + in-flight connection reuse at edge leads to mixed routing decisions when route tables are being swapped (commit window race).
Preliminary finding: Edge logs show route recompute events time-aligned with orchestrator commits. Affected sessions had lease remaining <15s at recompute time more frequently than control group.

Telemetry: No 5xx spikes in serving-runtime during windows; capacity levels nominal. KV cache misses increased ~12% for tenant during commit windows, which can trigger fallback to stateless variant (open-m-7b).
Reproducibility: Reproduced with synthetic load in staging using identical commit cadence; stutter windows appear when session-lease < 20s at commit time.
workaround: Increase session lease TTL for tenant to 300s and stagger commit windows (avoid committing weight change during many near-expiry leases). Customer applied lease extension and reported immediate reduction in mixed responses.
resolution_notes: Mitigation steps: (1) Disable route recompute on snapshot commit for leases with remaining_ttl < 30s (temporary safeguard); (2) Orchestrator patch to apply commit atomically with graceful drain window (PR linked below); (3) Edge fix to prefer existing session route until lease expiry rather than recomputing mid-flight. Target for full fix: 2026-03-18.
